subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: HPV pathogenesis, multimodal therapy, organ preservation and systemic immunotherapy

steps.tx: **Head and neck squamous** cell carcinomas arise from mucosal surfaces, with tobacco and alcohol driving oral cavity cancers and high-risk HPV16 driving **oropharyngeal cancers**. Keratinizing oral cavity lesions exhibit extensive TP53 mutations, whereas transcriptionally active HPV16 infection drives non-keratinizing oropharyngeal carcinomas arising within lymphoid crypts of the palatine and lingual tonsils.

left.title: HPV-Negative HNSCC
points: Etiology: Heavy tobacco and alcohol use
Anatomical sites: Oral cavity, larynx, hypopharynx
Poorer response to radiation and chemotherapy

right.title: HPV-Positive Oropharynx
points: Anatomical sites: Tonsil, base of tongue
Genetics: Wild-type p53; viral E6/E7 oncoproteins

steps.tx: The side section contrasts a pale **oral cavity** tumor tied to tobacco and alcohol with a bulky tonsil and tongue base mass tied to **HPV16**, framed as keratinizing versus nonkeratinizing disease. This matters because the lesson separates **tobacco driven** cancer with frequent TP53 change from virus driven throat cancer arising in lymphoid crypts with better treatment response.
steps.say: The image shows a sagittal head section with an oral cavity growth linked to tobacco and alcohol and a separate tonsil and tongue base growth linked to HPV16. It reinforces the lesson split between keratinizing oral cancer with frequent TP53 change and nonkeratinizing virus driven throat cancer with superior sensitivity to combined treatment.

steps.tx: HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer requires confirmation by strong, diffuse **p16 immunohistochemical** staining. In the **AJCC 8th edition** staging system, p16-positive oropharyngeal carcinoma carries a significantly more favourable prognosis than HPV-negative disease. Patients presenting with multiple cystic cervical lymph nodes maintain early stage designations and superior survival.

steps.tx: The tonsil nests show non keratinizing **oropharyngeal carcinoma** invading lymphoid stroma with strong diffuse **p16** staining of nuclei and cytoplasm. This block pattern marks transcriptionally active **HPV16** disease. Confirming p16 positivity matters because HPV driven cancer carries a more favorable outlook and follows distinct staging with superior response to combined treatment.
steps.say: This stain shows tonsillar carcinoma nests infiltrating lymphoid stroma with strong diffuse p16 positivity in nuclei and cytoplasm. Such block staining confirms HPV related oropharyngeal cancer. The lesson notes this group has a more favorable prognosis and its own staging system, so p16 testing directly shapes counseling and treatment planning.

vis.alt: Tonsillar carcinoma nests show strong diffuse p16 staining within lymphoid stroma.
vis.caption: Tonsillar cancer shows strong diffuse p16 block staining. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Definitive **concurrent chemoradiotherapy** utilizing high-dose **cisplatin at 100 mg/m2** administered every 3 weeks for 3 cycles represents the evidence-based standard of care for organ preservation in locally advanced laryngeal and pharyngeal cancers. High-dose cisplatin acts as a potent radiosensitizer, delivering superior locoregional control and overall survival compared to radiation therapy alone.

steps.tx: In locally advanced head and neck cancers requiring cytoreduction, induction **TPF chemotherapy** combining docetaxel, cisplatin, and continuous infusional 5-FU provides substantial tumour shrinkage. Delivering 3 cycles of induction TPF prior to definitive chemoradiation significantly enhances larynx preservation rates in advanced laryngeal cancer and reduces distant metastatic failure in locally advanced disease.

right.title: Clinical Efficacy & Risks
points: High risk of severe febrile neutropenia and mucositis

steps.tx: In recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer, the phase III **KEYNOTE-048** trial established **pembrolizumab** as standard first-line therapy. For tumours expressing a **combined positive score** of 1 or higher, pembrolizumab monotherapy significantly prolonged overall survival. Across total cohorts, combining pembrolizumab with platinum and fluorouracil chemotherapy produced statistically superior survival over standard chemotherapy.

steps.tx: In patients with locally advanced HNSCC who are medically unfit for high-dose cisplatin, the **Bonner regimen** combining definitive radiotherapy with the anti-EGFR antibody **cetuximab** represents a validated alternative. Cetuximab bio-radiotherapy significantly improves locoregional control and overall survival over radiotherapy alone without aggravating cytotoxic renal toxicity or ototoxicity, although acneiform skin rash is common.

steps.tx: Addressing global accessibility, a landmark Indian randomized phase III trial proved that **low-dose nivolumab** at a flat dose of 20 mg every 3 weeks combined with triple metronomic oral chemotherapy significantly prolonged overall survival in recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer. Adding low-dose nivolumab to oral methotrexate, celecoxib, and erlotinib doubled median overall survival, establishing a groundbreaking cost-effective immunotherapy strategy.

right.title: Metronomic Chemotherapy Alone
points: Standard palliative oral option in low-resource care

steps.tx: Following primary surgical resection for advanced oral cavity or laryngeal cancer, **postoperative concurrent chemoradiation** is indicated for high-risk adverse features. Landmark collaborative phase III trials **EORTC 22931** and **RTOG 9501** proved that microscopic positive surgical margins and extracapsular nodal extension represent the two definitive indications where adding concurrent cisplatin to postoperative radiation significantly improves locoregional control and overall survival.
